title: Spot pictures in chat nicknames

blocks.text: A chat service shows a warning when a nickname contains a picture (a face, a heart, a rocket), and prints each nickname over a dashed underline in its plain-text logs. Support has two reports: `agent_007` gets the warning, while a nickname ending in a rocket doesn't, and that nickname's underline comes out one dash too long.

Finish `hasPicture(nickname)` and `underline(nickname)` in `src/main/java/practice/Nicknames.java`. Letters of any script, digits, `#`, `*`, `_` and `-` are not pictures. Count a picture as one character, as the screen shows it; the tests use only pictures that are a single Unicode character. About two lines in total.

cases.says: letter-only nicknames have no picture, a heart is a picture, and the underline is one '-' per character
a picture stored as two chars, such as a rocket, is found
digits, '#' and '*' are not counted as pictures
a picture stored as two chars adds one '-' to the underline, not two

origin.section: isEmoji and StringBuilder.repeat Have Code-Point Overloads, and isEmoji Says Yes to Digits

concepts: Character.isEmoji and its siblings take code points, so chars() misses emoji outside the BMP; isEmoji is true for digits, '#' and '*', where isExtendedPictographic is not; StringBuilder.repeat(int, int) takes a code point.
